new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Spot-checked all four 'silent' supplementary works (JIPA ms, Bossers & Boone 2023, NLLT preprint + NLLT text, balafon paper) by a full-text search for stress/accent|accent|prominen|intonation|metrical|foot|feet|tonic: none says anything about word stress in Northern Toussian; the only hits are Bossers & Boone's tone-diacritic sentence (p. 8), the NLLT metrical-grid analogy (preprint p. 29) and 'intonational boundary tones'. The only stress-adjacent remark anywhere held by the project is Prost 1964's 'position inaccentuée' / 'ə atone' vowel-reduction note, which concerns Southern Toussian (wib) and was correctly excluded.

tone_statements.citation: Struthers-Young, Anthony. 2026 (ms dated May 7, 2026). Northern Toussian. Submitted to Journal of the International Phonetic Association (JIPA Illustration; Djigouera dialect). 38 pp. lingbuzz/010271
tone_statements.quote: Northern Toussian has three level tones: a high tone (á), mid tone (ā), and low tone (à). Additionally, it has six lexical contour tones, HM (a᷇ ), HL (â), LH (ǎ), LHL (ǎ`), LHM (ǎ¯), and HLH (â´), though the HLH contour is only attested in one word, bê´ ‘again.’ I analyze the contour tones as being comprised of two or more of the level tones. … Downstep is frequent in the language, and both H and M tones can be downstepped.
tone_statements.locator: section 'Tone', p. 18 (inventory and table); downstep sentence p. 24

tone_statements.citation: Struthers-Young, Anthony. 2024. Verbal grammatical tone in Northern Toussian. Oral presentation, 11th World Congress of African Linguistics (WOCAL 11), University of Nairobi. Presentation slides, 88 pp.https://www.anthonystruthersyoung.com/static/homepage/documents/ASY_WOCAL_2024_verbal_grammatical_tone_in_northern_toussian.pdf
tone_statements.quote: • The apva grammatical tone is a floating L tone • However, its realization is dependent on multiple factors, including • The tone of the target verb • The TAMP marker before the verb • The lexical properties of the verb • It is, therefore, a type of construct tune (Rolle 2018) [...] • (17) shows its effects with verbs of different tonal melodies • With H and HM tones, its effects are compositional • With a HL tone, it becomes L • M and L are unaffected
tone_statements.locator: slides numbered 37-38 ('Phonological properties' / 'Phonological distribution') (beamer overlay pages)
tone_statements.summary: Lexical verb melodies H, HM, HL, M, L (3 levels); floating L grammatical tone docks as contour or triggers downstep depending on TAMP marker and lexical class.

sources.note: Section 2.2 'Basic tonology' (pp. 2975-2976): three contrastive level tones H, M, L; CV syllables bear two- and three-tone contours; no consistent melody mapping in nouns; little declination in H/M sequences. The word 'stress' occurs only once, in a theoretical aside about metrical grids (Hayes 1995), not about Northern Toussian.

sources.note: Dedicated grammatical-tone study (conference slides, not a published paper). Verbs carry lexical melodies H, HM, HL, M, L; a floating L grammatical tone (glossed apva, 'absent preverbal non-subject argument') targets the verb when no non-subject argument immediately precedes it (argued NOT to mark intransitivity): H -> LH, HM -> LHM, HL -> L, M and L unaffected after past/irrealis/evidential markers; with other auxiliaries (negative, subjunctive) H verbs are instead downstepped; realization partly lexically conditioned; analysed as a construct tune (Rolle 2018).

sources.note: Slide 5 states the Kourinion NT system: 3 flat tones H, M, L and (potentially) 3 lexical contour tones HM, ML, LH, vowel length not phonemic. The talk describes vowel prolongation with tonal modulation (LH, resolving to H, or resolving to M) in six constructions at Kourinion (identificational 'it's X', WH questions, postverbal nominal complements, future, hypothetical conditionals, an imperfective alternative) versus only the identificational construction at Djigouera, and proposes a historical source for this grammatical tone.
